## Personality

A remarkably capable person, Mrs. Rachel Lynde manages her own affairs as well as those of others, maintaining a busybody presence while keeping a sharp, observant eye on everything that passes. Known as a red-hot politician, an active church worker, and a skilled sewer, she prides herself on being outspoken and always speaking her mind without fear or favor. Though her somewhat officious nature can lead her to be critical and easily shocked by any naughtiness, she remains at heart a kind, good soul who dearly loves to give advice. She considers herself a pretty good judge of human nature, though she holds pessimistic views about the world and firmly believes in foreordination. Endowed with strong, long-lasting opinions, she is notably farseeing, highly curious, and strongly opposed to higher education for women.

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde had brought up ten children and buried two, knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, and lived as neighbors with [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) for forty-five years without a quarrel. When [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) decided to adopt an orphan from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Rachel visited [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and warned [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) of the dangers. During a subsequent visit to meet the adopted girl, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Rachel offended her with blunt remarks about her red hair and looks, prompting a fiery outburst from the girl. After receiving a dramatic apology from [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Rachel completely forgave her and gifted her flowers. Rachel later advised [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) on how to handle Anne's school troubles, and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) confided in her after getting into trouble at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope). [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) later sought Rachel's help in purchasing and sewing a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves as a [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) gift for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md). Following Matthew's sudden death, Rachel praised Anne's growth, and she shared in the community's grief. As the years passed, Rachel kept up with local news, regularly exchanging gossip with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) about upcoming village events, town improvements, and new residents. When her husband [Thomas Lynde](../character/thomas-lynde.md) died, [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) invited Rachel to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) so she would not have to leave [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), an arrangement that enabled [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to step down from her teaching job to attend college.

## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 I An Irate Neighbor P38](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0038)

> "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P26](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0026)

> "Well, I wish you would. I guess we’ll have the supper in about a fortnight’s time. Uncle Abe Andrews is prophesying rain and storms for about that time; and that’s a pretty sure sign we’ll have fine weather."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P8](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0008)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--rachel-lynde.md)

Although listed as an enemy after early insults, Mrs. Rachel Lynde's relationship with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) quickly changed following an initial clash. When Mrs. Lynde made blunt remarks about Anne's hair and looks, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) reacted in a fiery rage before later offering a dramatic apology that Mrs. Lynde warmly accepted. Since then, Mrs. Lynde has served as an accessible neighborly advisor, offering counsel to [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) about handling Anne's temper and listening to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) express remorse over her mishaps.

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Rachel Lynde and [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) are close neighbors, friends, and tea companions who frequently consult one another on household matters and upbringing.
